data.title: Reddit shares plunge as Google's AI search squeezes traffic
data.description: Oct 30 : Reddit shares tumbled 29 per cent on Friday, marking their biggest single-day drop and hitting their lowest level in over a year, after the company warned that Google's AI-powered search was hurting referral traffic and could shrink its user base. The online discussion platform still appears in Google search results but is attracting fewer clicks, as users increasingly rely on the tech giant's AI tools for direct answers. "When more than a million search referrals a week disappear because Google's AI answers the question itself, investors are no longer looking just at the next three or four months, but at how much of Reddit's audience it will really own in the years ahead," said Vitor Madeira, senior market specialist at Capital.com. Reddit warned that its daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter if referral traffic kept declining. The trend is also hitting other businesses, including news publishers, educational platforms such as Chegg and travel and product-review sites. Meanwhile, shares of rival Pinterest fell nearly 8 per cent after it missed analysts' estimates for third-quarter revenue and profit, and forecast revenue for the crucial holiday quarter below estimates. If current losses hold, Reddit is set to lose more than $7 billion in market value and Pinterest about $900 million. The two stocks have fallen about 44 per cent and 23 per cent, respectively, this year through their last close. Reddit has a 12-month forward price-to-earnings ratio of 19.03, compared with Snap's 7.53 and Pinterest's 8.48, according to LSEG data. Separately, Reddit on Friday said it has extended its cloud services agreement with Google through 2029, committing to spend $580 million over three years. Google is also facing questions about monetization of AI-powered search, after growth in search revenue slowed to 12 per cent in the September quarter, sending Alphabet shares tumbling and wiping about $500 billion off its market value on Thursday. At least 11 brokerages cut their price targets on Reddit, and at least 13 did so on Pinterest.

data.title: Meta settles with teen during trial testing claims social media caused depression, eating disorders
data.description: Oct 30 : Meta Platforms has settled with a teen plaintiff who accused the company of designing Instagram and Facebook to be addictive, causing her mental health problems and disordered eating, attorneys for the plaintiff said on Friday. The settlement came after jury selection began on Wednesday for a trial that was slated to test the claims of two teens, identified as S.J. and K.D.B., against Meta and Snapchat parent Snap Inc. Meta had settled with S.J. days before the trial, so Friday's settlement with K.D.B. means the trial is expected to proceed against Snap only. “We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client,” Emily Jeffcott, an attorney for K.D.B., said in a statement. The trial is the second in Los Angeles state court over claims brought by young people who say they became addicted to social media after Meta, Snap, TikTok and Alphabet's YouTube designed their platforms to encourage compulsive use. S.J. and K.D.B. had previously settled with TikTok and YouTube. The case was selected among the thousands of pending lawsuits as a test case, so the jury's verdict could influence how the companies and plaintiffs resolve similar cases. S.J., a 16-year-old girl from Illinois, and K.D.B., an 18-year-old from Mississippi, say they began using YouTube as early as age 3 and the other platforms around age 9, developing compulsive habits they blame on features such as autoplay and infinite scroll.  The companies have rejected claims their platforms were designed to addict young people, and say they have taken action to make the apps safe places for young people to express themselves.  Social media companies face thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities alleging the companies knowingly sought to addict children to their platforms, contributing to a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression and suicide.  In the first case to go to trial, which ended in March, a Los Angeles jury found Meta and YouTube had been negligent and awarded a young woman $6 million in damages. The next two teens whose cases were selected for trials either settled or dropped their claims against the companies. The first school district chosen for trial settled with all of the companies. In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every state and US territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general over the platforms’ harm to teens and agreed to make changes to how Instagram and Facebook work for teens. Earlier this month, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty after a jury found the company misled Facebook users about the privacy of their data and how it handles hate speech. The company has said it will appeal.

data.title: Big Tech returns smallest share of cash to shareholders in 15 years, given AI spending
data.description: Oct 30 : The biggest US technology companies generated record amounts of cash in the first nine months of 2026, yet returned the smallest share of it to shareholders in at least 15 years as surging artificial intelligence spending squeezed share buybacks. The retreat threatens a long-standing source of support for technology share prices. With companies buying back fewer shares, investors are increasingly dependent on heavy AI investments delivering enough profit growth to justify their valuations. Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle returned 9.3 per cent of the cash their businesses generated as dividends and buybacks in the first three quarters of the year, down from 27.4 per cent a year earlier, a Reuters analysis of LSEG data and companies' financial reports showed. Operating cash flow actually rose 29 per cent from a year earlier to a record $542.9 billion. But capital spending, driven by the AI boom, doubled to $556.9 billion, exceeding the cash the five firms generated for the first time in data going back to 2011. That left them with a combined free cash flow deficit of $14 billion, against a surplus of $143.5 billion a year earlier. The squeeze has hit buybacks hardest. The five companies cut repurchases 83 per cent to $13.6 billion, from $81.8 billion a year earlier. BUYBACKS FIRST TO GO Dividends, which investors treat as a commitment, rose to $37 billion in the first nine months of 2026 from $33.9 billion a year earlier. Buybacks almost disappeared. Alphabet and Meta have not repurchased a share in 2026, after buying back $66.5 billion in the first nine months of last year. Amazon pays no dividend and has not bought back shares since 2022. Microsoft accounted for nearly all the five companies’ remaining repurchases, and cut its buybacks to $4.4 billion in the September quarter from $5.7 billion a year earlier. Some companies are no longer covering their payouts from what their businesses earn after capital spending. With combined free cash flow (FCF) negative, the five companies’ $50.6 billion in payouts was effectively funded from cash reserves, borrowing or share sales. Amazon’s capital spending of $75.9 billion in the third quarter was almost 80 per cent more than the $42.4 billion its operations generated, and it raised $48.1 billion of long-term debt in the quarter. Alphabet’s free cash flow was also negative, and it raised about $12.4 billion from share sales and $29 billion from debt. THE HIDDEN COST The loss of buybacks matters more than the dollar figures suggest, because buybacks have flattered per-share earnings for years. When companies buy back and retire their own shares, profits are spread across fewer shares, lifting earnings per share even when total profits do not grow. Alphabet reduced its share count by 9.5 per cent between the end of 2020 and 2025 through buybacks, ING said. That alone provided a boost of roughly 2 per cent a year to earnings per share (EPS), even without any increase in profits. Without that boost, per-share earnings must come from actual profit growth. That is a harder test, and it arrives just as depreciation charges on new data centres start to rise. It also lands where investors are most sensitive. Investors care “so much more about EPS than FCF,” Mark Schilsky, a technology sector specialist at JPMorgan, said in a client note last week. Technology and communication services stocks, which account for about 43.5 per cent of US market value, delivered a shareholder yield of just 0.28 per cent in July, against 1.99 per cent for the rest of the market, MSCI found. NO END IN SIGHT Amazon said it still expects about $220 billion of capital spending this year, and the other companies have signalled further increases. That leaves Big Tech shareholders with a different bargain from the one they signed up for, accepting less cash today in exchange for a bet that AI will eventually generate enough profit to make up for it. "For the last 15 years, companies increasingly returned excess capital to shareholders through buybacks and dividends," said Ehren Stanhope, co-head of investment management at Franklin Templeton. "The current regime may increasingly be characterized by greater equity and debt issuance, a request of capital from investors." (Reporting By Patturaja Murugaboopathy, Editing by Vidya Ranganathan and Nia Williams)

data.title: Nasdaq faces $2 trillion wipeout in October as AI spending fears deepen
data.description: Oct 30 : More than $2 trillion in market value is set to be wiped from the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 this month, as Big Tech earnings intensified investor scrutiny of whether the billions being poured into artificial intelligence can generate returns quickly enough. The wipeout would amount to slightly more than SpaceX’s entire market value. The index has fallen over 5.8 per cent so far in October as the AI trade ran into turbulence, with hyperscalers Meta Platforms, Alphabet and Amazon.com raising spending forecasts further as they race to expand AI infrastructure. The prospect of ever-bigger AI outlays has unnerved investors, particularly as rising borrowing costs threaten to make debt-funded investment more expensive and harder to justify. Here's a roundup of megacap earnings so far, with Apple set to report next week and AI bellwether Nvidia due mid-November. TECH WIPEOUT Alphabet suffered its biggest one-day percentage drop on record on Thursday after disappointing results in the core business of search advertising and a massive acceleration in cash burn. Meta's plans for a record $97.5 billion fund raise heightened concerns about shareholder dilution and whether mounting AI spending could force other Big Tech companies to increasingly tap capital markets. Microsoft and SpaceX broke from the gloom, with results that showed AI spending starting to pay off. "It may be that we've overestimated how strong the growth might be, but they're not going negative in aggregate," said John Bilton, global head of strategic research at Multi-Asset Solutions. "We have an insatiable and growing demand for data." RISING DEBT PILE Microsoft is reportedly planning to raise about $25 billion through its first US investment-grade bond sale in more than nine years. Among other hyperscalers, Meta, Amazon and Alphabet have issued hundreds of billions of dollars in bond sales over the past four years, worrying investors about overreliance on the medium for raising capital. Morgan Stanley forecast capital spending on AI infrastructure overall will surpass a trillion dollars next year. COST TO INSURE AGAINST DEBT DEFAULT SURGE AI companies’ growing reliance on debt funding is emerging as a new risk for investors, challenging the view that the companies at the heart of the boom are insulated from macroeconomic pressures. The concern is spreading beyond stocks to credit markets, where investors are starting to price in the possibility that rising financing costs, combined with slower returns on AI spending, could squeeze companies previously viewed as relatively insulated. ROBUST REVENUE Revenue across the "Magnificent Seven" has remained strong since ChatGPT's launch in 2022, showcasing insatiable demand and perhaps why investors were initially willing to back the spending, even as the timeline of payoffs remains uncertain. Amazon's cloud computing cash cow, Amazon Web Services, continued to accelerate, while Meta offered better-than-expected revenue growth and an upbeat outlook. Microsoft also forecast strong cloud growth in its latest earnings report. SOARING CAPEX Big Tech has historically spent heavily on infrastructure to build and expand businesses such as cloud computing, online advertising and e-commerce, but the AI boom has pushed capital expenditure to dizzying levels. J.P. Morgan expects global AI capex to reach $5.5 trillion by 2030, and sees $900 billion being spent in 2026 alone. This year's AI capex by Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle and Microsoft would likely equal their cumulative spend since the November 2022 launch of ChatGPT, J.P. Morgan analysts noted.

data.title: Strange beaked 'hell chicken' is the first fruit-eating dinosaur
data.description: WASHINGTON, Oct 30 : While dinosaurs ate a lot of different things, including each other, fruit long seemed to have been absent from their menu. But scientists now have found fossils of a turkey-sized and toothless dinosaur possessing a parrot-like head that exhibited multiple adaptations for a specialized fruit diet. This first-known frugivorous dinosaur, named Infernogallus jamesi, lived about 66 million years ago during the Cretaceous Period at the twilight of the age of dinosaurs and displayed traits on its beak and jaws for mashing soft food like fruit. It is known from fossils unearthed in Montana and North Dakota. The name Infernogallus means "hell chicken," a nod to its bird-like appearance and the fact that its fossils were found in the Hell Creek rock formation, which spans the US states of Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota and Wyoming and has yielded the remains of some of the most famous dinosaurs. It would have eaten fruit and other soft plants in the subtropical coastal floodplain ecosystem it shared with the likes of apex predator Tyrannosaurus, three-horned herbivore Triceratops and tank-like armored plant-eater Ankylosaurus. Infernogallus was about 5 feet (1.5 meters) long and weighed around 25 pounds (11.3 kg). While the fossils — one nearly complete skeleton and isolated bones from a jaw and palate — did not reveal feathers, the researchers believe Infernogallus was covered in them, based on fossils of close relatives. It belonged to a group called theropods that includes T. rex and all the meat-eating dinosaurs, as well as some that took to eating plants and the entire bird lineage. "This definitely expands the range of lifestyles we thought dinosaurs had, and it shows how adaptable theropods were," said paleontologist Greg Funston of Stony Brook University in New York, lead author of the research published in the journal Nature Communications. Fruits are the reproductive structures of angiosperms, also called flowering plants. Angiosperms first appeared earlier in the Cretaceous, around 130 to 140 million years ago, and subsequently took over landscapes previously dominated by plants called gymnosperms like conifers and ginkgoes. Infernogallus shows that some dinosaurs may have had a close ecological relationship with flowering plants. "It has been proposed before that some groups of dinosaurs ate fruits, but there was never evidence to back it up," said study co-author Thomas Dudgeon, a postdoctoral researcher at the Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto. "The discovery of Infernogallus shows that dinosaur diets were likely far more diverse than we previously thought. Prior to this discovery, there was a bit of a mystery in dinosaur evolution. The evolution of flowering plants introduced a brand-new food source that undoubtedly had consequences for the animals living alongside them," Dudgeon said. The fruit available for Infernogallus may have included various berries as well as drupes, a broad category that today includes types with a central pit like peaches and cherries as well as others like mangoes and olives. THREE KEY FEATURES Infernogallus showed a range of features indicating a frugivorous diet. The three most important, Funston said, were the organization of jaw muscles that powered back-and-forth chewing motions, a mobile joint that enabled the jaw to slide forward, and a series of ridges and grooves on the beak to help mash and shear soft plants like fruits. "We see these features separately in birds and turtles today that eat soft foods, like the fig-eating vulturine parrot or green sea turtles that chew soft sea grass. But no living animal has all three adaptations, showing just how specialized Infernogallus was," Funston said. Infernogallus also shows how adaptable beaks are compared to teeth. "Once you've lost your teeth and developed a beak instead, the range of foods available dramatically increases, including plants, as long as you have some way to digest them," Funston said. Most herbivorous theropods used stomach stones called gastroliths to grind food. But Infernogallus and other members of a lineage called caenagnathids chewed their food instead. Fruit-eating animals play an important role for angiosperms by dispersing seeds. "Mammals and birds would probably also have eaten fruit, but they didn't show the same kinds of specializations for a frugivorous diet that Infernogallus does, so it might have been a less important resource for them. Mammals and birds also were quite small in the Cretaceous, so it's unlikely that they were spreading very large seeds, or that they were spreading them big distances," Funston said. "We know that these big-seeded fruits were proliferating and spreading, and it seems like caenagnathids could have fit this role — although we feel more evidence is needed before drawing that link confidently," Funston said.

data.title: Kuaishou's Kling AI unit completes a near $3 billion funding round
data.description: Oct 30 : Tencent-backed Kuaishou Technology said on Friday that its unit Beijing Kling has completed a fundraising round of about 19.8 billion yuan ($2.98 billion). The short-video platform operator will hold two-thirds of the equity and 52.45 per cent of voting rights in the Kling AI maker through its Lucky Labs holding vehicle. • The fundraise comes after a $2.8 billion raise in July, which drew investors like Alibaba and Tencent, when Kling was valued at $15 billion pre-money • Kuaishou did not reveal how Kling would use the proceeds • Among new investors in the latest round: A unit of Hong Kong-listed Kingdee International invested 300 million yuan, Gongqingcheng Junke put in 200 million yuan and a unit of Shanghai-listed MetaX added 100 million yuan • They partially took over other investors' commitments and received redemption rights • Kling competes with AI video generation models of OpenAI, Google and TikTok owner ByteDance • Kling is planning for an IPO next year, Bloomberg News reported earlier this month citing people familiar with the matter ($1 = 6.66 Chinese yuan renminbi)

data.title: Intel on course for worst day ever, triggers global chip rout
data.description: Oct 30 : Intel tumbled 29 per cent on Friday and was on track for its sharpest one-day decline, deepening a broader retreat in technology stocks as investors grew increasingly wary of weakening PC demand and the vast spending required to build out AI infrastructure. The steep fall put the US chipmaker on track to shed more than $137 billion in market value, underscoring the challenges facing CEO Lip-Bu Tan's turnaround as a prolonged PC slump offsets heavy investments in AI and manufacturing expansion. Semiconductor stocks, including Advanced Micro Devices, Arm Holdings, Qualcomm, Nvidia, Broadcom and Micron, fell between 2 per cent and 10 per cent. "The market is in a sell first, ask questions later mood right now, and Intel's warning has given investors an easy excuse to take some money off the table across chip stocks," said Matt Britzman, senior equity analyst, Hargreaves Lansdown. The selloff spread to server makers, reflecting investor caution toward companies tied to the semiconductor and AI infrastructure supply chain. Shares of server makers Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Super Micro Computer fell between 6 per cent and 10 per cent. The STOXX Europe 600 Technology Index fell 2 per cent, with sector heavyweight ASML shedding 4.6 per cent. US-listed shares of TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, fell 3.3 per cent. Intel forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below analysts' average estimate of $17.07 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Finance chief David Zinsner also said Intel does not expect positive cash flow this year. MEMORY CRUNCH BITES Higher memory prices, driven by suppliers shifting capacity toward AI-focused high-bandwidth memory chips, are raising PC costs and weighing on already weak consumer demand. PC chips accounted for roughly half of Intel's third-quarter revenue, and the company expects sales from the segment to decline more than 20 per cent sequentially this quarter after a 5 per cent drop in the September period. "It will be important to see if Intel can expand the highly profitable Xeon product supply to help offset this developing weakness in PC," said Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management. "Bottom line, weaker sales volumes, higher manufacturing costs, and an out-of-cycle product mix is a recipe for the stock to decline over the near term as future earnings are under a lot of pressure."

data.title: Reddit plunges as Google AI search squeezes traffic
data.description: Oct 30 : Shares of Reddit tumbled 23 per cent in premarket trading on Friday after it warned Google's growing use of AI in search was hurting referral traffic and could shrink its user base, offering fresh evidence of AI-driven disruption. Pinterest also fell 7.28 per cent after forecasting fourth-quarter revenue below Wall Street estimates, as a pullback by cross-border sellers in Europe weighed on its outlook. Here are more details: • Reddit's warning highlights how Google's shift toward AI-powered search, which can answer queries directly, is disrupting the flow of traffic to websites that have traditionally relied on the search engine for users • Total daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from about 130 million if referral traffic continues to fall, Reddit said • JPMorgan analysts said the expansion of Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, along with changes to how machine-translated content is ranked, has pushed search traffic down • A reset in expectations is appropriate and the near-term outlook is increasingly clouded, said Piper Sandler analysts • Meanwhile, Reddit said in a filing it had extended its cloud services agreements with Amazon Web Services and Google through 2029, committing to spend $880 million and $580 million, respectively, over three years • Pinterest's third-quarter revenue of $1.17 billion missed analysts' estimates of $1.21 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG • Pinterest forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $1.425 billion to $1.475 billion, below Wall Street estimates • RBC analysts said changes to the EU's de minimis exemption hit cross-border sellers sooner and harder than expected, leaving Pinterest's European revenue flat • Reddit had fallen about 44 per cent this year and Pinterest about 23 per cent through Thursday's close • If current losses hold, Reddit is set to lose $5.7 billion in market value and Pinterest more than $800 million

data.title: Gone in 20 minutes: How the biggest heist in crypto history unfolded
data.description: SINGAPORE: Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance , the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record digital asset theft. WHAT HAPPENED? About US$6.3 billion of cryptocurrencies were drained from wallets that Binance uses to process transactions, according to the exchange and expert analysis of blockchain records. Binance said in a statement on X that it initially thought the attack involved a compromised laptop.  "However, our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," it added, without elaborating. The exchange operates a secure asset fund for users, a US$1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customers in the event of a security breach, according to its website. Co-CEO Richard Teng said losses would be covered by the fund and company resources. According to US blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs, the attackers compromised Binance's "signing infrastructure", which authorises transactions, allowing them to issue instructions that emptied the affected wallets. The bulk of the heist unfolded in about 20 minutes, blockchain records show, beginning shortly after 8pm GMT on Thursday (Oct 29). Once the funds were moved, the attackers raced to shift them beyond the reach of Binance counterparties and stablecoin issuers, which have frozen roughly half of the stolen assets. An unusual feature of some cryptocurrencies, including major stablecoins such as Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC, is that their issuers can freeze them remotely. "In layman's terms, the attacker may not have stolen the vault key, they may have hijacked the system that tells the vault to release money," said Joshua Chu, a Hong Kong lawyer who works on crypto cases.  WHO IS BEHIND IT?  Several US blockchain analysis firms said the attack bears similarities to previous operations attributed to North Korean hackers. Teng said Binance's investigation had not yet identified the attackers, while North Korea routinely denies involvement in cyberattacks and cryptocurrency thefts. North Korea's mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to requests for comment. TRM said the breach shared characteristics with last year's attack on crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korean hackers. The firm said it was highly confident the same group was behind the Binance theft. Chainalysis said funds stolen in an attack last month on Bitget were being mixed with proceeds from the Binance breach.WHERE'S THE MONEY? About half the stolen assets were stablecoins that have since been frozen by issuers including Tether, Circle, Ripple and World Liberty Financial, the Trump family's crypto venture. That doesn't mean the coins will be returned to Binance, but it significantly limits the attackers' ability to convert them into cash. TRM said some of the funds had already been posted as collateral to borrow ether and estimated that about US$2.4 billion worth of bitcoin and ether is beyond reach. "No company issues bitcoin or ether and no company can freeze either one," said Patrick Tan, general counsel of ChainArgos, a blockchain intelligence firm in Singapore. "The bitcoin and ether can be stopped only if the attacker sends them to a crypto-asset exchange or broker that is able and willing to freeze them, or if law enforcement obtains the private keys." Market participants said the attackers would likely mix the stolen coins with other assets or use lesser known coins and exchanges to try to move the proceeds. "The more time passes, the less likely they will be able to fold those funds into other exchanges or payment providers — they essentially get blacklisted," said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a stablecoin infrastructure company. "In reality a lot of the proceeds of hacks ... (can only be laundered) in the first few hours, but after that happens, you have a lot of different players who know those are marked funds ... and they usually sit there for years." WHAT NEXT? The theft is the latest in a series of major digital asset breaches. Attackers stole US$2.9 billion of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 incidents last year, according to TRM Labs. The attack has also rattled confidence in the sector. Cryptocurrencies fell on Friday and the total market value of stablecoins declined, suggesting investors were pulling money from digital assets.

data.title: Global equity funds draw inflows for a sixth straight week
data.description: Oct 30 : Global equity funds saw substantial inflows in the week ended October 28, though at a slower pace, as a rebound in AI and chip stocks, led by South Korea’s SK Hynix after record quarterly profit, lifted demand for technology and Asian funds. Investors bought a net $10.19 billion in global equity funds for a sixth consecutive week of net purchases, though inflows eased from $25.06 billion the previous week, according to LSEG Lipper data. There was, however, some caution in markets over the AI trade ahead of earnings reports from AI hyperscalers Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon. Asian equity funds led regional inflows, attracting $9.9 billion in net purchases, after $11.58 billion the previous week. Investors added $4.54 billion to European funds but withdrew a net $6.65 billion from US equity funds. Among sectoral funds, investors allocated $5.5 billion to the technology sector, up from $5.07 billion the previous week. Industrial sector funds also drew $408 million, while utilities saw $928 million in outflows. Weekly net inflows into global bond funds cooled to a six-week low of $2.72 billion. Global short-term bond funds saw $2.67 billion in weekly outflows—the first net sales since April 15—while investors bought $2.62 billion in government bond funds and $1.01 billion in corporate bond funds. Meanwhile, money market funds recorded net outflows of $38.5 billion, reversing from $16.95 billion in inflows the previous week. In commodities, investors withdrew $1.51 billion from gold and other precious metal funds, marking a second week of net sales in the past seven weeks. Energy funds, however, attracted $177 million in inflows. Data covering 29,184 emerging-market funds showed equity funds remained popular for a third straight week, drawing $2.2 billion in net inflows. Bond funds, however, saw net sales of $1.85 billion, their largest weekly outflow since September 30.

data.title: FBI and US Secret Service working with Binance after $6.3 billion hack, source says
data.description: LONDON, Oct 30 : Binance is working with law enforcement around the world, including the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and the United States Secret Service (USSS), after hackers stole a record $6.3 billion from the platform, a person familiar with the situation told Reuters. The US embassy in London said it had no comment. The USSS did not respond to a request for comment sent via email outside of US hours.

data.title: Explainer-Binance's $6.3 billion hack: How crypto insurance works
data.description: Oct 30 : Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the world's biggest crypto heist, putting a spotlight on how cryptocurrency exchanges insure their digital assets against theft and cyberattacks. But insurance protection is far from uniform. Coverage depends on how assets are stored, how hackers gain access and the specific terms of the policy. Limited regulation and volatile crypto prices have long made insurers wary of the sector, despite growing demand for protection against digital asset theft and claims against company executives. While both crime and demand for protection have tracked cryptocurrencies' meteoric rise, underwriting such risks remains a niche business offered largely by specialist insurers in the Lloyd's market and in Bermuda. WHAT IS DIGITAL ASSET INSURANCE? Digital asset insurance is a range of policies designed to protect cryptocurrency exchanges, custodians and other companies operating in the sector against financial losses arising from the theft of digital assets, cyberattacks, technology failures and other business risks. Unlike traditional insurance, these policies are tailored to risks associated with blockchain technology, including the theft or loss of private keys, wallet security breaches, smart contract vulnerabilities and failures in digital asset custody. The global crypto insurance market was valued at $9.37 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $184.98 billion by 2033, according to Data Bridge Market Research. The research firm cited growing institutional adoption of cryptocurrencies and rising incidents of cyberattacks and digital asset theft among the factors driving demand. Coverage can include several types of policies: • Crime insurance for theft, social engineering and scams • Cyber liability for breaches, hacks and regulatory response • Errors and omissions insurance for software bugs, smart contract failures • Directors and officers insurance for lawsuits targeting executives • Technology liability for infrastructure providers HOW ARE LOSSES COVERED? When a crypto exchange suffers a hack, losses can be covered through a combination of insurance payouts, the company's own capital and emergency funds set aside to compensate customers. The extent of insurance coverage depends on the policies held by the exchange, including their limits, deductibles and exclusions. Where losses exceed the insured amount, the company must rely on its own financial resources or other recovery arrangements to meet its obligations. Some exchanges also maintain reserve funds to reimburse customers following security breaches. Binance established the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) in July 2018 as an emergency reserve to protect users in extreme cases, such as security breaches or platform-level incidents. As of 2026, the SAFU fund holds crypto assets worth roughly $1 billion, entirely in bitcoin, according to Binance's website. The company did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment on its insurance coverage. WHAT CAN PREVENT AN INSURANCE PAYOUT? Exclusions that allow insurers to deny certain claims are common in policies covering digital assets as well as the personal liabilities of directors and officers at cryptocurrency companies. These can limit the scope of protection available to companies and make it harder for them to secure coverage. Common exclusions in these policies include value fluctuations, fraudulent acts by the policyholder and unsecured or negligent key management. DO TRADITIONAL CRIME AND CYBER INSURANCE POLICIES COVER CRYPTO? Most standard crime insurance policies do not cover cryptocurrency losses, as they were originally designed to protect physical property such as cash, securities and precious metals. Traditional cyber liability policies also do not always cover the value of digital assets stolen in a hack. While cyber policies can cover both first-party losses and third-party liabilities, including forensic investigations, customer notifications and legal expenses, they generally exclude the loss or transfer of funds. As a result, standalone cyber policies typically do not cover the full value of stolen cryptocurrency unless specific digital asset coverage has been added. HOW DO INSURERS ASSESS CRYPTO THEFT CLAIMS? Insurers examine how a breach occurred, which systems were compromised and whether the resulting loss falls within the policy's coverage. They may also assess whether the exchange followed required security procedures, including controls over private keys, wallet access and transaction approvals. The distinction between an external hacker stealing credentials and an employee deliberately transferring assets can determine whether a crime or cyber insurance policy covers the loss.

data.title: Cathay Pacific says Amadeus breach affected 53,000 bookings
data.description: Oct 30 : Hong Kong flagship carrier Cathay Pacific Airways said on Friday a data security breach at the Spanish software provider Amadeus affected around 53,000 bookings, though its own systems and operations were unaffected. Cathay joins other airlines, including Japan Airlines and South Korea's Asiana Airlines, that recently flagged customer data was compromised in the Amadeus breach. • The October 28 breach included booking reference, passenger name and flight details in most cases, but additional personal information was compromised in a smaller subset of cases, Cathay Pacific said • Cathay Pacific said the breach affected bookings from August 2023 to September, citing Amadeus data, and added there was "no evidence that financial or payment information was accessed" • It said Amadeus has taken actions to contain the incident and implemented enhanced monitoring and detection capabilities on its systems • Amadeus said it had become aware of a vulnerability affecting a travel booking display environment, but did not respond to a question on how many airlines and customers' data were affected • The investigations are ongoing and there are no indications that the vulnerability has been exploited for ransomware purposes, Amadeus added • Earlier this week, Japan Airlines said a similar breach affected the data of 92,000 customers due to unauthorized access to Amadeus' system

data.title: Reddit, Pinterest shares tumble on weak user and revenue growth
data.description: Oct 30 : Shares of Reddit and Pinterest fell in premarket trading on Friday, after Reddit warned that Google's AI search features could shrink its user base, and Pinterest forecast weak fourth-quarter revenue. Reddit shares tumbled 23 per cent, while Pinterest slumped 8 per cent. Here are more details: • Reddit said search engine referrals fell by more than 1 million on average each week in October • Total daily active unique visitors could fall by a low double-digit percentage in the fourth quarter from about 130 million if referral traffic continues to fall, Reddit added • JPMorgan analysts said the expansion of Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode, along with changes to how machine-translated content ranks, has pushed search traffic down • A reset in expectations is appropriate, and the near-term outlook is increasingly clouded, Piper Sandler analysts added • Reddit said in a filing it had extended its cloud services agreements with Amazon Web Services and Google through 2029, committing to spend $880 million and $580 million, respectively, over three years • Pinterest's third-quarter revenue of $1.17 billion missed the LSEG-compiled estimate of $1.21 billion • Pinterest forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $1.425 billion to $1.475 billion, below Wall Street estimates • RBC analysts said changes to the EU's de minimis exemption hit cross-border sellers sooner and harder than expected, leaving Pinterest's European revenue flat • Reddit had fallen about 44 per cent this year and Pinterest about 23 per cent through Thursday's close • If current losses hold, Reddit is set to lose $5.7 billion in market value and Pinterest about $900 million
